headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection and data leakage; both frameworks default to broad filesystem/network access with no isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and uses shared memory by default; LangGraph can also read/write application-defined files and persists state via a checkpointer store. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if one agent consumes the other's files or state as trusted input. No MCP/shared channel is documented, so this is interaction-based rather than universal.
conditions: IF CrewAI writes attacker-controlled text into the shared working directory and LangGraph later parses that text as instructions
IF LangGraph checkpointer state is exposed to CrewAI as trusted file content
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Disable automatic parsing of peer-generated files
Add provenance tags to shared artifacts
Review any file-to-prompt ingestion paths
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch developer-provided data and have broad network egress plus filesystem access. If they share a workspace or checkpointer-backed state, either can expose sensitive crew or graph state to model providers or tools. The profiles do not prove a mandatory leak, but the default surfaces make leakage plausible in ordinary deployments.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or shared checkpointer store
IF either agent forwards file contents or state to a model provider or external tool
mitigations: Use separate workspaces and credentials
Restrict outbound network destinations
Redact secrets before tool calls
Minimize shared state fields
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on agent I/O

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, subprocess spawning, and broad network egress. CrewAI writes the host working directory, while LangGraph can persist shared state via a checkpointer store; concurrent writes to the same mutable resources can race or corrupt state. The overlap is dangerous by default because neither profile shows locking or isolation.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared database without external locking
IF both agents mutate the same git or filesystem-backed artifacts through developer tools
mitigations: Assign disjoint write paths
Serialize writes with an external lock
Use separate checkpointer namespaces
Run each agent in its own container
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is a multi-agent orchestration framework with shared memory, and LangGraph is a stateful graph framework where node outputs can become later inputs. If one agent's output is fed into the other without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions. The profiles show the pathway exists, but not that it is unavoidable or automatically destructive.
conditions: IF CrewAI outputs are passed into LangGraph nodes without validation
IF LangGraph state is reused across turns as authoritative memory
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Require structured schemas for handoffs
Log and diff handoff payloads
Limit downstream actions to read-only review
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before execution

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source frameworks with no explicit residency, certification, or retention claims, so a compliance breach is not proven. The only concrete issue is that both handle developer-provided secrets/API keys and can persist state or files, which can create policy mismatch if the operator stores regulated data in shared state. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling model.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into shared agent state or persisted files
IF the deployment policy requires retention or residency guarantees that are not configured
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of agent state
Set short retention on logs and checkpoints
Document data handling boundaries
Use separate secrets stores
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
